rv.q: Bringing together romance, humor and swashbuckling swordfights, this is a production not to be missed.

As fun as the production elements of 'yo ho.' are, it's hard to call this an unqualified success when the leaner, meaner, one-act version of this play haunts its current iteration like the Flying Dutchman.
But I kept wishing for more order in this production so I could follow what was happening and to whom.
This constant-humor approach does limit the nuance of character relationships that can be developed; however, it does not mean that the show was void of emotionally moving moments.
As it stands, it's a charmingly diverting evening at the theater. But with some work, this could be a frothy comic gem.
Although Babes' swashbuckling and a committed cast support this show's production, 'yo ho' gets bogged down in the storytelling.

They wear heavy boots, striped pants, with a beard across their face. Nothing seems amiss here, pirates have swords and no one has time to shave when there is much plundering, pillaging, and looting to be had. But looking closer, that shadow of a beard really isn’t that good of a fake beard at all, almost too obvious of a fake beard.
In all, the acting and directing are great, but SMJ's story is a zero.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this queer pirate tale about Anne Bonny and Mary Read, with some praising its swashbuckling fun and representation while others find it raunchy, confusing, and straying too far from the historical story.
